probability.basis: Prefer one household: James Glasgow, indexed with Agnes Waitte at Polwarth on 18 June 1663, is probably the James who fathered the Gordon children John (1666), Patrike (1667), Jean (1671), Robert (1673), Agnes (1676) and Margrat (1679). The father’s repeated full name, the neighbouring Berwickshire parishes, the first child three years after marriage and the orderly thirteen-year child sequence form a coherent family. The daughter Agnes supplies modest naming support; it is not the deciding evidence. The maintained 1702 Gordon marriage citation for Jean also names father James, adding a compatible adult continuation for her. Read together, these favour a single local family over six isolated fathers or an unrelated Polwarth couple. No concrete competing contemporary Gordon James household has been identified in the maintained material. That is the scope of this comparison, not a claim to have exhausted the population. The child indexes explicitly name James as father but omit the mother. Their named-father roles are documented for the record-defined children; identifying that father with the 1663 Polwarth husband is probable. Agnes Watt is separately assessed as probable mother of all six children on the marriage, locality and sustained family sequence. This is an inference, not literal maternity in the indexes; a later marriage or another local James remains possible. Jean’s later marriage and the later adult identities of John and Patrick remain separately assessed. Patrick’s proposed Kilclone son and migration, James’s own John Glasgow-1084 ancestry and the unrelated Kilwaughter James are not strengthened. No original register image was newly inspected: this review combines the previously accepted index entries and maintained citations.

wikitree_update_relationship_changes.subject: Jean Glasgow, 1671 Gordon child
wikitree_update_relationship_changes.scope: Named father and child in the Gordon baptism index; Polwarth husband identity probable and later adult identifications separate
wikitree_update_relationship_changes.explanation: Prefer one household: James Glasgow, indexed with Agnes Waitte at Polwarth on 18 June 1663, is probably the James who fathered the Gordon children John (1666), Patrike (1667), Jean (1671), Robert (1673), Agnes (1676) and Margrat (1679). The father’s repeated full name, the neighbouring Berwickshire parishes, the first child three years after marriage and the orderly thirteen-year child sequence form a coherent family. The daughter Agnes supplies modest naming support; it is not the deciding evidence. The maintained 1702 Gordon marriage citation for Jean also names father James, adding a compatible adult continuation for her. Read together, these favour a single local family over six isolated fathers or an unrelated Polwarth couple. No concrete competing contemporary Gordon James household has been identified in the maintained material. That is the scope of this comparison, not a claim to have exhausted the population. The child indexes explicitly name James as father but omit the mother. Their named-father roles are documented for the record-defined children; identifying that father with the 1663 Polwarth husband is probable. Agnes Watt is separately assessed as probable mother of all six children on the marriage, locality and sustained family sequence. This is an inference, not literal maternity in the indexes; a later marriage or another local James remains possible. Jean’s later marriage and the later adult identities of John and Patrick remain separately assessed. Patrick’s proposed Kilclone son and migration, James’s own John Glasgow-1084 ancestry and the unrelated Kilwaughter James are not strengthened. No original register image was newly inspected: this review combines the previously accepted index entries and maintained citations.
